facts.raw_span: a 4-month history of worsening headaches
complete right homonymous hemianopia
a left occipital intracerebral hematoma of unknown cause
Noncontrast head CT showed a left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage
a left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage
suggesting a cavernous angioma
Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells forming masses with branching ectatic vasculature
focal collagenous regions, and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields
strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1
scattered S100-positive cells
negative staining for CD34, EMA, desmin, muscle-specific actin, and Bcl-2

concepts.why: The histopathological examination and immunohistochemical studies support this diagnosis, with features such as spindle cells, branching ectatic vasculature, and strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1.
The presence of spindle cells, focal collagenous regions, and strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, as well as scattered S100-positive cells, are consistent with this diagnosis.

The initial suggestion of a cavernous angioma and the presence of a left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage could be consistent with a meningioma, although the histopathological examination does not support this diagnosis.
The initial suggestion of a cavernous angioma based on imaging findings, although the histopathological examination does not support this diagnosis.

The presence of spindle cells, branching ectatic vasculature, and strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, as well as up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields, could be consistent with this diagnosis, although the overall clinical and histopathological picture is more suggestive of a hemangiopericytoma.
